points.description: Set a pointer to the first element of the array (pointer initialized to the array name/address of first element), then access elements by adding the index/offset to the pointer, i.e. *(ptr + i) or *(array + i).
points.partial_credit: 2 marks if only one half is stated (pointer to first element, or adding an index/offset) or the idea is vague or has a minor error.

points.description: States that the index/offset is added to (increments) the pointer to reach the element, with dereferencing to get the value, e.g. *(p + i).
points.partial_credit: 0.5 if offset addition is mentioned without dereferencing or clear link to the index.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a pointer is set to the array's first element and the index/offset is added to it (e.g. p = arr; *(p+i)), in any wording. Part marks for only one half, or a vague or slightly wrong version. No marks for describing ordinary arr[i] subscripting or unrelated pointer facts without the pointer-plus-offset idea.
